Hannah (CS): Sparrow Health procurement asked for a short SLA + onboarding blurb for their RFP packet. They want: MUP name, p50/p95/p99 latency targets, how credits are calculated (simple example), and a 1-page onboarding timeline. Renewal check in ~7 weeks. Can @Ethan and @Priyanka confirm numbers so I can draft?
Ethan (SRE): quick numbers: Hosted MUP = 99.9% (we call it "monthly uptime percentage"). Typical latency targets: p50 = 130ms, p95 = 380ms, p99 = ~1000ms (tail varies with long-context requests). Dedicated commit we offer = 99.96% MUP. Note: initial model warm-up and KV cache population can push p95/p99 higher for ~30-90 minutes after deploy.
Priyanka (Solutions): agreed. Suggested plain-language line for the doc: "Latency SLOs measured on steady-state traffic. Transient deviations during initial rollouts, model swaps, or cache warm-ups are expected and documented in onboarding guidance."
Hannah (CS): credits: procurement wants a single formula they can paste plus a worked example. Keep it plain.
Ethan (SRE): we have a slightly different cap we can offer here: ```credit = round(min(0.2, max(0, (SLO_target - observed_MUP) / SLO_target)) * committed_monthly_fee, 2)``` cap = 20% of monthly committed spend for this RFP.
Priyanka (Solutions): worked example to paste: "Committed spend = $9,500/mo; Target MUP = 99.9%; Observed MUP = 99.7% -> shortfall = 0.2% -> credit = min(20%, 0.002/0.999) * $9,500 ≈ $19.02. Credits are applied as invoice credits on the next billing cycle."
Marcus (AE): Sparrow flagged bursty batch jobs at midnight. Recommend mentioning optional mitigations: reserved concurrency (dedicated pool), scheduled pre-warm window (1hr), and priority lanes for critical routes. Also note Dedicated provisioning lead time = 2 weeks if they want reserved capacity.
Hannah (CS): action items: (1) Ethan - paste the monitoring query/dashboard link we can reference and confirm multi-region note; (2) Priyanka - draft the one-pager + small table (Hosted vs Dedicated) with p50/p95/p99 and add-ons; (3) Marcus - prepare add-on bullets + pricing range and sync renewal owner. I'll consolidate and send to procurement by Thursday COB.
Ethan (SRE): metric name confirmed: "monthly uptime percentage (MUP)". Example PromQL to compute availability over 30d: `sum_over_time(up{service="inference-api"}[30d]) / (30*24*3600)` . We'll attach a dashboard snapshot (will share link) and a short note: multi-region customers receive per-region SLOs; aggregated reporting is available but credits are calculated per-region unless contract says otherwise.
Priyanka (Solutions): drafting now. Onboarding timeline (compact): Day 0: kickoff + API keys; Day 1: integration smoke tests + sample traffic; Day 3: performance tuning + canary; Day 7: scale to steady-state. Optional accelerated 3-day ramp with pre-warm slot if scheduled in advance.
Marcus (AE): I'll draft pricing bullets for reserved concurrency and the 1-hour pre-warm add-on; will also propose a proactive health check during the first 14 days of ramp as part of renewal conversation.
Hannah (CS): please drop final snippets into https://redwood.docs/sparrow/sla-onboard-draft by Wednesday 09:00 PT. ReminderBot: ping thread at 2024-05-10T09:00:00Z. :white_check_mark:
ReminderBot: Reminder scheduled 124 2024-05-10T09:00:00Z for thread participants.
Ethan (SRE): small legal ops note: include the sentence "SLA credits are the sole and exclusive remedy for availability shortfalls unless otherwise agreed in writing." I'll add that to the draft doc.
Hannah (CS): thanks all — I'll assemble and add procurement-friendly table before sending.
